title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
statement: There are `n` cities and `flights[i] = [from, to, price]`. Return the cheapest price from `src` to `dst` using **at most `k` stops** (so at most `k + 1` flights), or `-1` if no such route exists.

example.why: With one stop the only route is 0 → 1 → 3 for 100 + 600. The cheaper 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 (400) needs two stops.

idea: Plain shortest-path search ignores the stop limit: the cheapest route may simply use too many flights.

So build the answer by **number of flights**. Start with only `src` reachable (cost 0). Each round allows **one more flight**: every flight `u → v` may extend a route that reached `u` in the previous round.
Run `k + 1` rounds. The updates of a round are written to a **copy**, so a route cannot chain two new flights within the same round.

complexity.timeWhy: k + 1 rounds; each one copies the n prices and looks at all E flights once.

steps.text: Our example input is drawn on the stage. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
